title: Ciscomani recognized for bipartisan and effective work in Congress, highlights Arizona results
text:
Ciscomani recognized for bipartisan and effective work in Congress, highlights Arizona results
M. K. Barron
U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani has been recognized as one of the most bipartisan and effective members of Congress, earning the highest Bridge Score among Arizona’s congressional delegation, according to an Aug. 26 announcement from his office. Ciscomani said his focus remains on delivering results for Arizonans on issues such as water, veterans, public safety, national security, and economic development.
"My focus from day one has been to deliver common-sense, lasting results for my constituents in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District," Ciscomani said. "That means working with anyone willing to find solutions, regardless of party. From preserving our water to protecting public lands and advocating for veterans, my job is to get things done. I'm proud of my record of successfully bringing federal funds to the communities I represent—funds to support our first responders in Huachuca City and Oro Valley, as well as to expand workforce training and improve our roads. These are real wins that will directly improve the quality of life in southeastern Arizona."
This latest recognition builds on previous accolades during Ciscomani's first term when the nonpartisan Center for Effective Lawmaking named him the most effective member of Arizona’s congressional delegation and ranked him 15th among all members of the U.S. House in the 118th Congress. In the current session (119th Congress), he received an "A" grade and a Bridge Score of 97.5 out of 100 from Bridge Grades—an organization that evaluates lawmakers based on third-party data focused on bipartisan legislation.
According to the Center for Effective Lawmaking, Ciscomani introduced 32 substantive bills during this session; nine passed through the U.S. House of Representatives. Legislative priorities have included policies affecting southern Arizona residents with a focus on veterans' issues and water security.
One key legislative accomplishment is passage through the House by unanimous voice vote—and advancement through Senate committee—of H.R. 6380 (the Chiricahua National Park Act), which would designate Chiricahua National Monument as a national park.
"Washington is full of career politicians who talk a good game about problems but go radio silent when it comes to finding real solutions," said Ciscomani. "The hardworking people I represent deserve leaders who are willing to work with anyone, roll up their sleeves and do what’s necessary to score tangible wins." Water security remains central: The Colorado River Caucus was launched with Rep. Joe Neguse; bipartisan legislation has advanced regarding federal water monitoring and conservation efforts; H.R. 5770 (the WATER Data Improvement Act) passed both chambers and became law in 2024.
Ciscomani is set to secure $42.7 million across five counties within his district: Cochise, Graham, Greenlee, Pima, and Pinal.
Juan Ciscomani has served in Congress representing Arizona's 6th District since replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023; he was born in Hermosillo, Mexico in 1982 before moving to Tucson where he currently lives; he graduated from University of Arizona with a BA in 2005, according to Congressman Juan Ciscomani's official website.
